# the contributor audit: action closure, dyadic filtering and sharp energy–cap comparison


conclusion. This audit records the independent root checks after Registry118.

## 1. Exact action addition has the old strict-response dual

Sources: `candidate 85a041ec649c5375`,
Sections7–9, and
`candidate 61c2a6c203bcade2`.

The physical gaps ell_i(u,z)-u.x are nonnegative on the ENTIRE canonical
hull, since they are affine and nonnegative on every generating fiber.
For a fixed finite L, max_(i,u)[V_i-L gap_i]_+ is a finite continuous
nonnegative convex function in the physical coordinates. On the hull it
is uniformly bounded independently of L. At a regular measured boundary
point, every zero gap has the unique actual fiber normal; compactness of
the index set then gives monotone convergence to the contact-max speed.
Surface L1 convergence follows, including d=1 endpoint counting.

The actual-section support roof is concave in the real base, so its cuts
with this one convex potential are actual convex erosions. Inner homothets
keep the original measured fibers positive. Each L is fixed before the
erosion parameter tends to zero; a finite strict response margin transfers
by first selecting finite L and then selecting the erosion size. There is
no unjustified uniform remainder or interchange of limits. Conversely,
support planes touching every original base realize each old roof field
exactly at the measured fibers. The boundary-L1 closures and all finite
linear-response polar duals agree.

The disk neutral-response warning is correct. Its error's odd first
moment is strictly negative at every finite L by the strict triangle
inequality, and the exact centroid gauge formula gives a strictly
negative normalized retained-mass response at the prescribed old mark
velocity. The source correctly does NOT claim that no other potential
realizes the original speed; an affine potential does. Its separate arc
example distinguishes exact continuous traces, not finite response sets.

## 2. Dyadic identities and the precise arithmetic obstruction

Source:
`candidate 9f68cd8c98117884`.

The contracted-fiber formula follows by solving the integer base equation.
The pushforward factor is exactly 2^(-kd); first displacement moments
have the additional factor 2^(-k). Closed arbitrary halfspaces retain
the scaled threshold, so pure-base boundary mass and oblique caps are
included. Tonelli and compact support justify the valuation generating
identities. These identities keep different cap and moment weights.

Pooling parity classes uses the half lattice. Relabeling them back adds
the explicitly displayed class-dependent base-normal threshold and may
leave the body. The Bezout argument proves that radial lattice positions
are precisely multiples of 1/gcd(z-p). A primitive positive-volume fiber
is therefore immobile under inward ray-supported transport whose output
is absolutely continuous for original mixed volume. This does not assert
that arbitrary aggregate cap-preserving couplings must be pointwise radial.

The reflexive-simplex product's displayed cap contains its own Gamma_d
portion and one outer fiber. Its dyadic mixtures have the stated exact
mass and cap fractions, strictly below ordinary Gamma_d despite exact
centering. The strict numerical inequality Gamma_d>1/(d+1) for d>=2 can
also be checked immediately from Gamma_d>1/e and e<3<=d+1. No ordinary
uniform-body theorem applies to these mixed centered measures.

## 3. Ordinary energy–cap bound, with its exact constant

Source:
`candidate 5f5575d4f9e40719`.

The root originally proposed the cone comparison; Defect independently
derived and wrote the full proof. Reading the complete source confirms
the following steps without an unproved localization assertion.

The actual section at height zero and any highest point supply the
homothetic subcone proving B<=b. Concavity of the section root and matched
positive mass give the positive-then-negative crossing, including a
possible downward jump at a supporting facet. The same concavity forces
the actual negative section density below the untruncated comparison
cone. Truncation at its uniquely matched lower height consequently gives
a second positive-then-negative crossing. The two restricted laws each
have exactly the same mass as their cone counterparts.

For alpha<=Gamma_d the computed cone optimizer has c<=0, so its inverse
affine power is increasing. The actual upper endpoint bound makes its
denominator positive on the whole original body, including any extra
negative extension. Stochastic comparison is in the correct direction.
The explicit beta integral yields

    E_K(y)/|K| <= ((d+1)^(d+1)/d^d) alpha(1-alpha^(1/d)).

This holds for ANY through-source cap of fraction alpha<=Gamma_d.
The first energy inequality does not require that the source be the
centroid of its zero section. Such axiality occurs only in equality.
Strict kernel monotonicity forces the exact conical section profile;
section convergence and equal-volume containment prove the actual cone
classification. Horizontal stationarity is equivalent to axiality.
The sharp cone cap's GLOBAL minimality follows from the already proved
inequality and strict increase of F_d, so it is not circular.

The d=1 interval formula, inverse-depth bound, and second derivative
constant ((d+1)/d)^(2d+1) all agree exactly. The square-root corollary
has coefficient 2d/(d+1) after factoring Gamma_d, as stated. The ordinary
centroid case also recovers the ordinary Gamma_d lower bound directly.

This quantitative ordinary theorem has not yet been converted into a
mixed mass-payment or integer-point selection theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
